about: How a seat is said inside a sentence (Fable B's ruling, Nov 11, on #8750): a seat on a body by the body ("run for the Mutual Village Council", then "the council"), a single office by its title in lower case ("run for mayor"), a district's seat with its district. Read by seatSaid in src/english/journal-words.ts. Above the town (Words lead, Nov 14, rule 100): a district's seat in Congress is "Congress in the 3rd District", a state chamber's "the state Senate in the 17th District", the U.S. Senate "the U.S. Senate"; a county's or town's district seat stays "commissioner in District 1". A body named for its members is said by one member after the first mention, with no article: "alderman" for the Board of Aldermen (Words lead, Nov 14); a body named as a body keeps its name ("the board").
